shortDescription: Indonesian state utility Perusahaan Listrik Negara has replaced its chief executive, the company's commissioner said on Thursday, following a series of power outages across the country in recent months.

children: Indonesian state utility Perusahaan Listrik Negara has replaced its chief executive, the company's commissioner said on Thursday, following a series of power outages across the country in recent months.

PLN at a shareholder meeting on Wednesday decided to remove Darmawan Prasodjo and appoint the firm's former risk management director Suroso Isnandar as CEO, its independent commissioner Andi Arief told Reuters
Indonesia's power outages have included a major blackout across at least six provinces in Sumatra in May and rolling outages in Java and Kalimantan in June and July
The latest outage was in Batam on Monday, lasting at least 16 hours
Asked if the leadership change was about the blackouts, Andi said no reason was given at the meeting
"I suspect this is a routine change, since Darmawan has been in the role for quite a long time," Andi said
